findings.reason: citing the two in-module/in-package mechanisms forces the plan to extend `_plan_documents` (a shared path lister both consumers call) and to place or extend the process runner knowingly instead of adding parallel ones.
findings.text: velocity.py:306 `_plan_documents` already performs the identical `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> -- <prefix>` listing the plan proposes to add as a new public sources reader on the same module, and reckon/service.py:206 `_run` already is a text-mode, never-raising, CompletedProcess-returning process runner of exactly the shape §13 proposes; the plan's runner census counted only git-named runners and names neither

findings.reason: the section must state the runner's byte/text mode and how each wrapper preserves its contract, or the "one runner" claim is false and two invocations survive.
findings.text: §13's "one process runner, with raising wrappers over it" cannot hold: it fixes the base runner at text mode, so velocity.git, whose contract is bytes and whose call sites (velocity.py:308, 795, 804, 835) call `.decode()`, is not a wrapper but a re-implementation that re-encodes the runner's text; a single runner serving routing._git's text output and velocity.git's byte output needs a stated mode/encoding the section does not give

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §12 sources reader hides the ls-tree invocation, the prefix scoping, the .py filter and the utf-8-sig decode behind one call, and §13's cache_root(kind) hides a five-kind by two-ordering table plus the unknown-kind refusal behind a kind name.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan names velocity as the owner to extend for both the runner and the cascade and retires the forks into it (pick_input_cache_root public, clones._git, clones._cache_root, clones.revised_python), so the duplicates it touches are consolidated rather than forked.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 states its net public_definitions change (+1 sources reader, -1 revised_python = zero) and §13 states its (+1 runner, +1 cache_root, -1 pick_input_cache_root = +1), and neither adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched git runners and cache cascades thoroughly and cites velocity.git/read_blobs/velocity_cache_root, routing._git, interface_counts.read_trees and the five cascade owners, but it proposes a revision-sources listing reader that duplicates the ls-tree pattern already at velocity.py:306 (_plan_documents) and a process runner whose shape already exists at service.py:206 (_run), neither cited.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §13 declares one text-mode runner and says velocity.git is "expressed as a wrapper over that runner", but velocity.git returns bytes (its callers at velocity.py:308, 795, 804, 835 call .decode()), which a text-mode CompletedProcess cannot supply.
